faq.question: What is JSONPath?
faq.answer: JSONPath is a query syntax for selecting values or nodes from a JSON document. It provides selectors for the root, object properties, arrays, wildcards, recursive searches, slices, and filters, depending on the dialect and evaluator.

faq.question: Which JSONPath specification does this tool support?
faq.answer: This page uses its own evaluator for a documented subset of JSONPath: `$`, `.name`, `['name']`, `[index]`, `*`, `..name`, and simple filters such as `[?(@.price < 10)]`. It does not implement the full RFC 9535 standard: array slices, unions, regular expressions, and functions are not supported. Expressions outside the subset are reported as invalid instead of returning partial results.

faq.question: What is the difference between a syntax error and no matches?
faq.answer: A syntax error means the expression cannot be parsed or uses unsupported syntax. No matches means the expression is valid under the evaluator but does not select any node in the supplied JSON. These cases require different fixes.

faq.question: What are common JSONPath expressions?
faq.answer: Examples include $.user.name for a nested property, $.items[0] for the first array item, $.items[*].id for every item ID, $..price for recursive price searches, and $.items[?(@.price > 10)] for a filter when filter syntax is supported.

faq.question: What does $ mean in JSONPath?
faq.answer: The dollar sign usually represents the root of the JSON document. For example, $.users starts at the root and selects the users property.

faq.question: What does .. mean in JSONPath?
faq.answer: Recursive descent searches descendants below the current location. For example, $..id can match id properties at multiple nesting levels, depending on the evaluator's semantics.

faq.question: Does the tool support filters?
faq.answer: Yes, with a limited set of comparison operators: `==`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, and `>=`, for example `$.store.books[?(@.price < 10)]`. Regular expression filters and function calls are not supported and are reported as invalid expressions.

faq.question: Does the tool support array slices?
faq.answer: No. Slice expressions such as `$.items[0:3]` are not supported by this evaluator, and neither are unions such as `$.items[0,2]`. Use a wildcard with a filter, or select the indexes you need one at a time.

faq.question: Why do I get duplicate-looking results?
faq.answer: Different nodes can contain the same value. Inspect the concrete match path, JSON Pointer, or source location to distinguish them instead of relying only on the displayed value.

faq.question: Can I see where each result came from?
faq.answer: If path reporting is enabled, each match can include its concrete JSONPath location and possibly an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer. This is useful when identical values appear in several parts of a document.

faq.question: Can I use JSONPath to modify JSON?
faq.answer: This page is designed for querying and extracting values. JSONPath itself is primarily a selection syntax; modifying the selected data requires a separate transformation or update operation.

faq.question: Can I use it with API responses?
faq.answer: Yes. Paste a valid API response and use JSONPath to inspect fields, arrays, nested objects, and filter results. The evaluator only queries the data supplied to the page and does not know the API's business semantics.

faq.question: Can I test large JSON documents?
faq.answer: The practical limit depends on document size, nesting depth, array length, evaluator complexity, result count, and browser memory. Filters and recursive searches may require more work than direct property access.

faq.question: Is my JSON uploaded to a server?
faq.answer: This page is designed to parse and query JSON in your browser without requiring a server upload. You should still avoid entering passwords, API keys, access tokens, private customer data, or confidential production payloads into any browser-based tool.

faq.question: Is this a free JSONPath tester?
faq.answer: Yes. You can paste JSON, test supported JSONPath expressions, inspect matches and paths, and copy the results without creating an account.

article.title: How to Test JSONPath Expressions Online
article.content:
What Is JSONPath?

JSONPath is a query syntax for navigating and selecting data from JSON documents. It is commonly used to find nested properties, array items, matching records, and values inside API responses or configuration files.

JSONPath implementations are not all identical. Some tools follow the newer IETF JSONPath RFC 9535, while others implement older or library-specific dialects. A reliable tester should identify the syntax it supports rather than implying that every JSONPath expression works everywhere.

How to Use a JSONPath Tester

  1. Enter JSON: Paste a valid JSON object or array into the document editor.
  2. Write an expression: Start with $ and add property names, array indexes, wildcards, recursive selectors, slices, or filters supported by the evaluator.
  3. Evaluate: Run the query against the parsed document.
  4. Classify the result: Determine whether the expression is invalid, valid but has no matches, or returns one or more nodes.
  5. Inspect paths: Review the concrete path, JSON Pointer, value, and node type when available.
  6. Copy the query: Reuse the tested expression in application code, API tests, a pipeline, or documentation.

Common JSONPath Expressions

  • $: Select the root document.
  • $.user.name: Select a nested property with dot notation.
  • $["user-name"]: Select a property whose name requires bracket notation.
  • $.items[0]: Select the first item in an array.
  • $.items[*].id: Select the id property from every item.
  • $..price: Search for price properties recursively.
  • $.items[?(@.price > 10)]: Filter items when predicate syntax is supported.

Dot Notation and Bracket Notation

Dot notation is concise for ordinary property names:

$.store.book[0].title

Bracket notation is useful for property names containing spaces, hyphens, punctuation, or characters that are not convenient in an identifier:

$["user profile"]["display-name"]

Use the notation supported by the evaluator and quote property names exactly as they appear in the JSON.

Wildcards, Recursive Descent, and Slices

A wildcard selects multiple children, while recursive descent searches below the current location. Array slices select a range when supported:

  • *: Match children or array items.
  • ..: Search descendants recursively.
  • [0:3]: Select a slice when the evaluator supports slice syntax.

Recursive queries can return many nodes, especially in large documents. Review match paths rather than assuming that every value with the same key belongs to the same logical object.

Filter Expressions

Filters let you select array items based on a condition, such as:

$.store.book[?(@.price < 10)].title

Filter syntax and available functions vary between JSONPath implementations. Comparisons involving missing properties, null values, strings, and numbers should be tested against the actual evaluator.

Match Values Are Not Enough

Two nodes can return the same value but represent different locations:

{"users":[{"id":1},{"id":1}]}

A useful result view should show both the value and its path, such as $.users[0].id and $.users[1].id. An RFC 6901 JSON Pointer can provide another precise location format for integration with tools that use JSON Patch or pointer-based updates.

Invalid Expression vs No Match

These results are different:

  • Invalid expression: The parser cannot understand the query or the evaluator does not support part of its syntax.
  • No match: The expression is valid but does not select a node in the current document.
  • Successful match: One or more values or nodes were selected.

Keeping these states separate makes debugging much faster. A syntax error should be fixed in the expression, while a no-match result usually requires checking property names, array indexes, document structure, or filter conditions.

JSONPath and JSON Pointer

JSONPath is a query language that can select multiple nodes. JSON Pointer, defined by RFC 6901, identifies one location using slash-separated tokens such as /users/0/name. They solve different problems and should not be presented as interchangeable syntax.

JSONPath in API Testing

JSONPath is useful for checking API responses, extracting fields, and writing assertions. For example, a test can verify that $.data.items[*].id returns expected identifiers. The exact expression syntax must match the API testing tool or library used by the project.

Implementation and Compatibility

Before copying a query into production code, test it in the target library. A query that works in a browser tester may fail in a tool that uses a different JSONPath dialect, function set, filter syntax, or result model. If the page implements RFC 9535, include the specification version and supported extensions in the reference.

Large JSON Documents

Direct property access is usually cheaper than recursive searches and complex filters. For large documents, result rendering can become as important as evaluation. A Web Worker, lazy filtering, virtualized results, and a result limit can keep the interface responsive.

Browser-Based Privacy

This tester is designed to parse and evaluate JSON in the browser instead of sending the document to a remote service. That is useful for development payloads and private configuration samples, but it is not a secret-management system. Avoid entering credentials, tokens, private customer information, or production secrets into any online tool.

faq.question: 什么是 JSONPath？
faq.answer: JSONPath 是一种用于在 JSON 文档中定位节点的查询语法，作用类似 XML 的 XPath。`$.store.books[0].title` 这样的表达式可以选中某个具体的值，也可以一次选中一组节点。

faq.question: 这个工具支持哪一套 JSONPath 规范？
faq.answer: 本页面使用自带的求值器，支持一份明确说明的 JSONPath 子集：`$`、`.name`、`['name']`、`[下标]`、`*`、`..name`，以及 `[?(@.price < 10)]` 这类简单过滤。它没有实现完整的 RFC 9535：不支持数组切片、并集、正则和函数。超出该子集的表达式会被判定为非法，而不是返回部分结果。

faq.question: 语法错误和没有匹配有什么区别？
faq.answer: 语法错误表示表达式无法解析，或使用了本求值器不支持的语法；没有匹配表示表达式合法，但在当前 JSON 里没有选中任何节点。前者要改表达式，后者要检查数据或路径。

faq.question: 有哪些常用的 JSONPath 表达式？
faq.answer: 常见写法包括：`$` 取根、`$.store` 取子对象、`$.store.books[0]` 取数组元素、`$.store.books[*].title` 取所有书名、`$..price` 递归查找所有 price、`$.store.books[?(@.price < 10)]` 按条件过滤。

faq.question: JSONPath 里的 $ 是什么意思？
faq.answer: `$` 表示文档根节点，几乎所有表达式都以它开头。相对写法里的 `@` 则表示过滤表达式内部的当前节点。

faq.question: JSONPath 里的 .. 是什么意思？
faq.answer: `..` 是递归下降操作符，会在整棵树的任意深度查找匹配的名称，例如 `$..price` 会返回所有名为 price 的节点。递归范围较大时请留意结果数量。

faq.question: 支持过滤表达式吗？
faq.answer: 支持，但只支持有限的比较运算符：`==`、`!=`、`<`、`>`、`<=`、`>=`，例如 `$.store.books[?(@.price < 10)]`。正则过滤和函数调用不支持，会被判定为非法表达式。

faq.question: 支持数组切片吗？
faq.answer: 不支持。`$.items[0:3]` 这类切片语法本求值器不处理，`$.items[0,2]` 这类并集也不支持。可以改用通配符配合过滤，或逐个选择需要的下标。

faq.question: 为什么结果看起来有重复？
faq.answer: 递归下降和通配符会遍历多条路径，同一个值可能通过不同路径被选中；过滤表达式也会对每个候选节点分别求值。通常改用更精确的路径即可消除重复。

faq.question: 可以看到每个结果来自哪里吗？
faq.answer: 可以。每个匹配都会显示它的 JSONPath、等价的 JSON Pointer（RFC 6901）以及节点类型，便于回到源文档定位，或在其他工具里复用该路径。

faq.question: 可以用 JSONPath 修改 JSON 吗？
faq.answer: 不可以。本工具只做查询和求值，不提供写入、删除或更新节点的能力。

faq.question: 可以用于接口返回的 JSON 吗？
faq.answer: 可以。把接口响应粘贴进来即可验证表达式；表达式确认后再写进代码里使用。

faq.question: 可以测试很大的 JSON 文档吗？
faq.answer: 实际可处理的规模取决于浏览器内存和设备性能。递归下降和通配符会遍历大量节点，文档很大时求值会变慢。

faq.question: 我的 JSON 会上传到服务器吗？
faq.answer: 解析和求值都在你的浏览器本地完成，不需要上传服务器。但仍不建议在任何浏览器工具中输入密码、API 密钥、令牌或机密数据。

faq.question: 这个 JSONPath 测试工具免费吗？
faq.answer: 免费，且无需注册账号。你可以粘贴 JSON、求值表达式并复制结果。

article.title: 如何在线测试 JSONPath 表达式
article.content:
什么是 JSONPath 测试工具？

JSONPath 测试工具用来验证一条表达式在给定 JSON 文档上到底选中了什么。它会返回匹配到的值，以及每个匹配在文档中的位置，避免把未经验证的表达式直接写进代码。

不同实现对 JSONPath 的支持范围并不一致，因此在一个工具里能跑通的表达式，换到另一个库里可能报错或结果不同。使用时应以目标库实际支持的方言为准。

常见使用场景

  • 接口调试：从接口响应里快速取出关心的字段，确认路径写法。
  • 日志排查：在结构复杂的日志 JSON 里定位嵌套字段。
  • 脚本预演：把要写进脚本的表达式先验证一遍，减少反复试错。
  • 数据核对：确认某个字段在整份数据里出现了几次、分别在哪里。

如何使用

  1. 输入 JSON：粘贴 JSON 或打开 .json 文件。
  2. 写下表达式：例如 `$.store.books[*].title`，也可以点选常用路径。
  3. 执行求值：点击求值按钮或按回车。
  4. 核对结果：查看匹配值、JSONPath、JSON Pointer 和节点类型。
  5. 复制复用：复制表达式或结果，写进文档或代码。

本页支持的语法子集

  • $：根选择器。
  • .name 与 ['name']：按名称取子节点，两种写法都支持。
  • [index]：按下标取数组元素。
  • *：通配符，选中所有子节点。
  • ..name：递归下降，在任意深度查找该名称。
  • [?(expr)]：简单过滤，支持 ==、!=、<、>、<=、>=。

不支持数组切片、并集、正则匹配和函数调用。遇到这些语法时会提示表达式非法，而不是返回不完整的匹配。

语法错误与无匹配

这是两种不同的失败：语法错误说明表达式本身无法解析或用了不支持的语法，需要改表达式；无匹配说明表达式合法，但当前 JSON 里没有对应节点，需要检查数据结构或路径写法。把两者分开提示，可以避免把数据问题误判成语法问题。

JSONPath 与 JSON Pointer

JSONPath 是查询表达式，可以一次选中多个节点；JSON Pointer（RFC 6901）是定位单个节点的路径表示，例如 `/store/books/0/title`。本页同时给出两种表示，方便在只接受 Pointer 的工具里继续使用。

需要留意的限制

  • 方言差异：本页是明确说明的子集，不是完整 RFC 9535 实现。
  • 只做查询：不提供修改、删除或写入节点的能力。
  • 递归代价：递归下降和通配符会遍历大量节点，大文档上会变慢。
  • 类型展示：节点类型只做基本区分（object、array、string、number、boolean、null）。

浏览器本地处理与隐私

解析和求值都在你的浏览器中完成，不需要把 JSON 上传到远程服务，适合接口响应和日志片段这类内容。但它不是密钥管理方案，请勿在浏览器工具中粘贴密码、API 密钥、访问令牌或生产环境的敏感数据。
